Computing Consumer Tech Space & Aerospace Earnings Menu Money & Markets Economic Indicators Markets Personal Finance Earnings Menu Lifestyle Cars & Bikes Collecting Entertainment Food & Fine Dining Health and Fitness Real Estate Travel General Trivia Connecticut's average Social Security check beats Mississippi's by $418.64 a month 
 Average Social Security check by state compared for 10 states at either end of a ranking of all 50 states and D.C., using December 2025 retired-worker data
 1 / 12 List slides Connecticut's average Social Security check beats Mississippi's by $418.64 a month List slides Previous Start over By Colleen Cabili · Updated November 3, 2026 Add QZ to Google Illustration: Quartz
 Retirees in Connecticut and Mississippi receive checks calculated by the same federal formula. The typical payment in each state still lands far apart. Connecticut's average retired-worker benefit was $2,308.36 in December 2025. Mississippi's was $1,889.72. That is a gap of $418.64 a month.
 The figures come from Table 5.J6 of the Social Security Administration's Annual Statistical Supplement, 2026. The table reports the average Social Security check by state for retired workers as of December 2025. It has 51 rows, one for each of the 50 states and one for the District of Columbia.
 At that point, 53,624,664 retired workers were collecting benefits nationwide. Their average monthly payment was $2,071.30. The national median was $1,991.90. The median marks the midpoint, with half of beneficiaries above it and half below. It can order states differently than the average does, and at the top of this table it does.
 This article covers 10 of those 51 rows: the five states with the highest averages and the five with the lowest. The high group is Connecticut, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Delaware and Maryland. All five sit in the Northeast or Mid-Atlantic. The low group is New Mexico, Kentucky, Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi. Four of those five are in the South.
 The selection leaves out the states with the most retired-worker beneficiaries. California had 5,341,103. Florida had 4,191,491, Texas had 3,710,457, New York had 3,000,986 and Pennsylvania had 2,319,503. Together those five states account for 18,563,540 people, or 34.6% of the national total. None of them falls among the five highest or five lowest averages.
 Each state slide that follows gives the average monthly payment, the median and the number of retired workers receiving benefits. It compares those figures with the national numbers from the same month. An individual check depends on lifetime earnings and the age at which a person starts claiming. The table itself does not explain why any one state lands where it does.
 A separate, later figure tracks the national average. The average retired-worker check was $2,087.52 in August 2026. That figure covers a different month. The state comparisons here use December 2025 throughout.
 Connecticut has the highest average Social Security check 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Connecticut retirees collected an average Social Security retired-worker benefit of $2,308.36 in December 2025, the highest of any state or the District of Columbia. Connecticut is also the only state in the table with an average above $2,300.
 Connecticut's lead at the top is narrow. Kiplinger points out that its average sits just $10.66 above New Hampshire, the second-highest state, at $2,297.70. Over a full year of checks, that monthly edge adds up to $127.92. Maryland, the fifth-highest state at $2,257.51, trails Connecticut by $50.85.
 The gap with the country as a whole is far wider. Kiplinger also notes that Connecticut's average is $237.06 above the national average of $2,071.30. Over 12 months, a check at Connecticut's average totals $27,700.32. A check at the national average totals $24,855.60 over the same stretch. The annual difference comes to $2,844.72.
 The median ranks Connecticut one spot lower. Its median retired-worker benefit was $2,248.90, second in the country behind New Jersey's $2,255.90. New Jersey's median edges Connecticut's by $7.00. Connecticut's median runs $59.46 below its average. When an average sits above the median, the largest checks in the group pull the average upward.
 Against the national median of $1,991.90, Connecticut's median is $257.00 higher. On that measure, the state's margin over the country is wider than its lead on the average.
 Connecticut had 606,612 retired-worker beneficiaries in December 2025. That is about 1.1% of the 53,624,664 retired workers receiving benefits nationwide. Among the five states with the highest averages, Connecticut's count trails New Jersey's 1,406,793 and Maryland's 892,917. It exceeds New Hampshire's 277,320 and Delaware's 206,680. Connecticut's total is about 2.2 times New Hampshire's.
 State tax rules also affect how much of each payment a retiree keeps. Connecticut taxpayers whose federal adjusted gross income reaches the cutoff for a full exemption on Social Security income may still qualify for a partial exemption.
 New Hampshire ranks second for average retirement benefits 
 Illustration: Quartz
 New Hampshire retirees collected an average Social Security check of $2,297.70 in December 2025. That was the second-highest average among the 50 states and D.C. Only Connecticut's average was higher, by $10.66.
 The gap below New Hampshire was even narrower. New Jersey ranked third with an average of $2,287.75, which left it $9.95 behind. Just $20.61 a month separated first place from third.
 New Hampshire's average sat $226.40 above the national average retired-worker benefit of $2,071.30. Its median of $2,214.90 was $223.00 above the national median of $1,991.90. The state's average was also $407.98 higher than Mississippi's, the lowest in the country.
 New Hampshire has a small retiree population compared with the other two states at the top. It had 277,320 retired-worker beneficiaries, the fewest among the three states with the highest averages. Connecticut had 606,612, more than twice as many. New Jersey had 1,406,793, about five times New Hampshire's count. New Hampshire's beneficiaries made up about 0.5% of the 53,624,664 retired workers nationwide.
 Measured by median, New Hampshire slips from second to fourth within the top-five group. Its median trailed New Jersey, Connecticut and Delaware. Only Maryland, at $2,180.90, had a lower median among the five states with the highest averages.
 The two measures can rank states differently because they respond to different parts of the distribution. An average adds up every check and divides the total by the number of beneficiaries. Every dollar counts toward it. A relatively small number of large checks can pull it upward. The median depends only on which check sits in the middle. Larger checks at the top do not move it in the same way.
 In New Hampshire, the average ran $82.80 above the median. Across the U.S., the national average exceeded the national median by $79.40. New Hampshire's spread was $3.40 wider than the national one. The table does not break down which checks produced that spread.
 New Jersey pays the highest median Social Security benefit 
 Illustration: Quartz
 New Jersey has the highest median Social Security retired-worker benefit in the U.S., at $2,255.90 a month in December 2025. Its average check, $2,287.75, ranks third among the 50 states and D.C.
 On the median, New Jersey edges out Connecticut, whose midpoint benefit is $2,248.90. The gap is $7.00. Connecticut leads the average ranking at $2,308.36, which is $20.61 above New Jersey's figure. New Hampshire sits between them on averages, in second place at $2,297.70.
 Delaware, New Hampshire and Maryland complete the top five by median, at $2,224.90, $2,214.90 and $2,180.90, respectively. New Jersey climbs two places from its average rank to its median rank. No other state in the high group moves up more than one place.
 New Jersey's median sits $264.00 above the national median. Its average runs $216.45 above the national average. Its median is also $465.00 higher than Mississippi's $1,790.90, the lowest median in the country.
 The distance between New Jersey's own average and median is $31.85. The national average exceeds the national median by $79.40. New Jersey's narrower spread means its average sits closer to what the retiree in the middle of its distribution receives.
 New Jersey's gap is the narrowest in the high group. Connecticut's spread is $59.46, Delaware's is $48.87, Maryland's is $76.61 and New Hampshire's is $82.80.
 New Jersey also has the most retired-worker beneficiaries among the five states with the highest averages, at 1,406,793. That exceeds the combined 1,090,612 in Connecticut, New Hampshire and Delaware. Maryland is next in the group, with 892,917. New Jersey's count equals about 2.6% of all retired workers receiving benefits nationwide.
 The state had a net exodus of retirees, according to Hire a Helper's report The New Retirement Map: Where Retirement-Age Americans Moved in 2025 and Why. The report examines where retirement-age Americans relocated during 2025 and why.
 Delaware retirees collect the fourth-highest average benefit 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Delaware's retired workers received an average Social Security check of $2,273.77 in December 2025. That ranked fourth among the 50 states and D.C., $202.47 a month above the national average.
 A year of checks at Delaware's December 2025 average would total $27,285.24. The same 12 checks at the national average would total $24,855.60. That is a difference of $2,429.64, assuming payments held steady all year.
 Delaware had 206,680 retired-worker beneficiaries, the fewest of the 10 states in this selection. That is about 0.39% of all retired-worker beneficiaries in the U.S. New Hampshire, the next-smallest of the 10, had 277,320. Maryland, fifth in the high group, had 892,917, more than four times Delaware's count.
 Delaware moves up one place on the median measure. Its median benefit of $2,224.90 ranks third in the country, behind New Jersey and Connecticut. Connecticut's median, second in the country, is $24.00 higher. Delaware's is $233.00 above the national median. New Hampshire, which edges Delaware on the average, falls behind it on the median.
 Delaware's average exceeds its median by $48.87. The national gap between the two measures was $79.40. Delaware's pair of figures sits closer together than the national pair.
 Delaware's average falls within a tight band at the top of the table. It trails New Jersey's $2,287.75 by $13.98 and leads Maryland's $2,257.51 by $16.26. Connecticut, in first place, is $34.59 ahead. Mississippi, at the bottom of the table, averages $384.05 less per month.
 Delaware's checks are set by the same national rules that apply in every state. The calculation begins with a primary insurance amount, the benefit payable at full retirement age. That age falls between 66 and 67, depending on birth year. A retiree who claims at full retirement age receives 100% of that amount. These rules describe how any check is calculated. They do not explain Delaware's position in the ranking.
 Maryland rounds out the top 5 for Social Security payments 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Maryland has the fifth-highest average Social Security check among the 50 states and D.C., at $2,257.51 a month for retired workers in December 2025. That puts the state $186.21 above the national average of $2,071.30.
 Maryland's median benefit was $2,180.90. It beat the national median of $1,991.90 by $189.00. That is a slightly wider margin than the state's lead on the average.
 The Maryland median also cleared the national average, by $109.60. Within the state, the average and the median sat $76.61 apart. That gap is wider than Connecticut's, where the two figures differ by $59.46.
 By median, Maryland also ranks last among the five states with the highest averages. The other four reshuffle when that group is sorted by median. Maryland is the only one whose position within the group does not change.
 The spread among the leading states is narrow. Maryland's average trails Delaware's $2,273.77 by $16.26. It sits $40.19 below New Hampshire's $2,297.70. It falls $50.85 short of Connecticut's $2,308.36, the highest average in the table. At the other end of the ranking, Maryland's figure is $367.79 above Mississippi's $1,889.72, the lowest. It also sits $302.84 above New Mexico's $1,954.67, the fifth-lowest average.
 Maryland also has a large retiree base. The state counted 892,917 retired-worker beneficiaries, about 1.7% of the 53,624,664 nationwide. That count is more than four times Delaware's 206,680. Among the five highest-average states, only New Jersey had more beneficiaries, with 1,406,793.
 At Maryland's December 2025 average, 12 monthly checks would total $27,090.12. The same 12 checks at the national average would come to $24,855.60. The difference is $2,234.52 over a year. That is an illustration at a fixed monthly rate, not a reported annual figure.
 Maryland's position fits a regional pattern. Kiplinger reports that average benefits run highest in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. Maryland and its neighbor Delaware are both Mid-Atlantic states, and both rank among the five highest averages. The source does not tie Maryland's rank to any state-specific cause.
 New Mexico has the fifth-lowest average Social Security check 
 Illustration: Quartz
 New Mexico retirees received an average Social Security retired-worker benefit of $1,954.67 a month in December 2025, the fifth-lowest figure among the 50 states and D.C. The state's median benefit was $1,825.90.
 That average sits $116.63 below the national average for the same month. The gap widens at the midpoint. New Mexico's median trails the national median by $166.
 Over a full year, the difference adds up. Twelve checks at New Mexico's December average would come to $23,456.04. The same 12 checks at the national average would total $24,855.60. That is $1,399.56 more.
 The distance grows against the top of the ranking. Connecticut's average check, the highest in the table, is $353.69 larger than New Mexico's.
 New Mexico had 366,403 retired-worker beneficiaries in December 2025. That is the smallest count among the five states with the lowest averages. Kentucky, Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi each had more retired workers drawing benefits. Kentucky's total of 719,046 is nearly twice New Mexico's.
 The state's average runs $128.77 above its median. That is the widest average-to-median spread among the five lowest-ranked states. Louisiana comes closest at $119.25, while Kentucky's spread is $77.23. The national spread in December 2025 was $79.40.
 A mean that sits well above the median points to a smaller group of larger checks pulling the average up. Half of New Mexico's retired workers received $1,825.90 or less. For a typical payment in the state, the median is the closer measure.
 That spread also shifts New Mexico's place within the low group. Its median ranks below Kentucky's $1,875.90 and Arkansas's $1,841.90, even though both of those states have lower averages. Only Louisiana and Mississippi post lower medians than New Mexico among the five.
 New Mexico is the one state in the bottom five located outside the South. It sits in the Southwest. That fits a low group that is mostly, but not entirely, Southern.
 Kentucky's average retirement benefit ranks fourth from the bottom 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Kentucky retirees collected an average Social Security retired-worker benefit of $1,953.13 in December 2025. That figure ranks fourth-lowest among the 50 states and the District of Columbia.
 Kentucky sits just behind New Mexico, the fifth-lowest state, whose average was $1,954.67. The difference between the two is $1.54 a month. In the ranking, the two states are nearly level.
 The gap with the national average is far wider. Kentucky's average falls $118.17 short of the U.S. average for the same month. Over 12 months, that adds up to $1,418.04 less than a check at the national average would pay.
 Kentucky places higher on the median than on the average within its group. Its median benefit was $1,875.90, the highest among the five states with the lowest averages. Arkansas came next at $1,841.90, $34.00 behind Kentucky. New Mexico's median was $1,825.90, Louisiana's was $1,807.90 and Mississippi's was $1,790.90. Kentucky's median still sits $116.00 below the national median.
 Kentucky's own average runs $77.23 above its median. When an average exceeds the median, the larger checks in a state's distribution lift the mean above the midpoint.
 The state also has the largest pool of retired-worker beneficiaries in the low group. In December 2025, 719,046 retired workers in Kentucky drew benefits. That is more than Louisiana's 661,928, the next-largest count among the five lowest-average states. It is also 352,643 more than New Mexico, the state just above Kentucky in the average ranking.
 Kentucky checks are sized under the same national rules that apply in every state. A person born in 1960 or later who starts benefits at 62 receives 30% less than the benefit payable at full retirement age. Waiting until full retirement age pays 100% of that amount.
 The December 2025 table does not show how many Kentucky retirees claimed early. The rules explain how individual checks are sized, not why the state's average lands where it does.
 Arkansas retirees receive the third-lowest Social Security average 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Arkansas has the third-lowest average Social Security retired-worker check in the country, at $1,932.29 a month in December 2025. That places it 49th among the 50 states and the District of Columbia.
 The state's median benefit was lower, at $1,841.90. That leaves a gap of $90.39 between the two measures.
 A median below the average means the higher checks in the state pull the average above the midpoint. For a typical retiree in Arkansas, the median is the closer guide to a monthly deposit.
 Both measures trail the national figures for the same month. Arkansas falls $139.01 a month short of the U.S. average retired-worker benefit. Its median sits exactly $150 below the national median.
 The monthly shortfall equals about 6.7% of the national average. Over a full year, the gap in averages adds up. Twelve months at the Arkansas average comes to $23,187.48. The same 12 months at the national average comes to $24,855.60. The difference is $1,668.12.
 Arkansas sits in a tight cluster near the bottom of the table. Its average is $5.14 above Louisiana's, which ranks second-lowest. It is $42.57 above Mississippi, the lowest in the country. Kentucky, one spot higher, averages $20.84 more.
 The distance to the top is wider. Connecticut's average, the highest in the table, runs $376.07 a month above the Arkansas figure.
 Arkansas had 513,912 retired-worker beneficiaries in December 2025. That is just under 1% of all retired workers collecting benefits nationwide. Among the five lowest-average states, that count trails Kentucky and Louisiana but tops Mississippi and New Mexico.
 Social Security sets each retiree's check from that person's own work history. Lifetime earnings are a central input in the calculation. Higher earnings over a career generally lead to a larger monthly benefit.
 Those rules work the same way in every state. A state's average is the total of its retirees' individual checks divided by the number of retirees.
 Louisiana has the second-lowest average Social Security payment 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Louisiana retirees collected an average Social Security retired-worker benefit of $1,927.15 a month in December 2025. That is the second-lowest average among the 50 states and D.C., ahead of only Mississippi.
 The state's figure sits $144.15 below the national average for the same month. Over a full year, a $1,927.15 monthly check adds up to $23,125.80 before any deductions.
 Louisiana's nearest neighbors in the ranking sit close by. Arkansas, with the third-lowest average, comes in just $5.14 higher at $1,932.29. Mississippi's average trails Louisiana's by $37.43. The distance to the top is far wider. Connecticut, the highest-average state, paid retired workers $381.21 more a month on average.
 Louisiana's median benefit was $1,807.90, which is $119.25 below the state's own average. When a mean sits above the median, a smaller number of larger checks pulls the average above the typical payment.
 Louisiana's midpoint is $184.00 below the national median. Among the 10 states covered in this list, only Mississippi posts a lower median, at $1,790.90.
 The state counted 661,928 retired-worker beneficiaries in December 2025. That is the second-largest total among the five lowest-average states, behind Kentucky's 719,046. It is more than Mississippi's 493,663 and Arkansas's 513,912.
 A state average blends hundreds of thousands of individual records into one number. Two retirees in the same state can collect very different amounts.
 Claiming age is one factor a worker controls. For each month a person waits past full retirement age, the benefit grows by two-thirds of 1%. That works out to 8% for each full year of delay. The credits stop growing at age 70.
 Full retirement age is 67 for anyone born in 1960 or later. Waiting from 67 to 70 adds three years of credits, or 24% on top of the full benefit. A worker due $1,000 a month at full retirement age would collect $1,240 by claiming at 70. The table does not show how many Louisiana retirees chose that route.
 Mississippi pays the lowest average and median Social Security check 
 Illustration: Quartz
 Mississippi ranked last in the nation for retired-worker Social Security benefits in December 2025. Its average check was $1,889.72 and its median was $1,790.90. Both were the lowest figures among the 50 states and D.C.
 The average falls $181.58 short of the national average for the same month. Across 12 monthly payments, that shortfall comes to $2,178.96. The gap on the median is larger. Mississippi's midpoint benefit sits $201.00 below the national median.
 Finishing last on both measures sets Mississippi apart from the top of the table, where the leader changes. Connecticut has the highest average, while New Jersey has the highest median. New Jersey's median sits $465.00 above Mississippi's.
 Louisiana comes closest on the median. Its figure of $1,807.90 is $17.00 higher than Mississippi's.
 On the average, Mississippi sits a clear step below its nearest neighbor. Louisiana, the second-lowest state, averaged $1,927.15. That is $37.43 more than Mississippi. No other pair of adjacent states in the bottom five is separated by as much. The next-widest gap, between Arkansas and Kentucky, is $20.84.
 The state had 493,663 retired-worker beneficiaries. That is about 0.92% of the national total. Among the bottom five, only New Mexico has fewer.
 Mississippi's median sits $98.82 below its average. At least half of the state's retired workers therefore receive less than the state average. A smaller share of larger checks pulls the mean upward. That spread is narrower than Louisiana's $119.25 and New Mexico's $128.77. It is wider than Kentucky's $77.23.
 Louisiana, Arkansas and Kentucky join Mississippi in the bottom five, and all three are in the South. New Mexico is the one state in that group outside the South.
 Mississippi does not tax Social Security benefits. CNBC reports that eight states do: Colorado, Connecticut, Minnesota, Montana, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Vermont and Utah.
 Mississippi does levy an income tax. It exempts retirement income, provided the taxpayer meets retirement plan requirements. Pension income is not taxed by the state either.
